title: Bresaola con Rucola e Grana
author: Marco Bellini
desc: Delicate, air-dried beef from the Valtellina valley, sliced paper-thin and dressed simply with peppery arugula, shaved Parmigiano, olive oil, and lemon.
longDesc: Bresaola is beef that's salted and air-cured for months in the cool alpine air of Valtellina, resulting in a lean, deep red cured meat with a delicate flavor best allowed to shine through minimal, bright accompaniments.
steps: Arrange the bresaola slices in a single layer on a serving platter.
Scatter the arugula evenly over the bresaola.
Drizzle generously with olive oil and a squeeze of lemon juice.
Finish with a crack of black pepper and serve immediately.
chefTips: Bring the bresaola to room temperature briefly before serving for the best flavor.
A good vegetable peeler works well for creating thin, even Parmigiano shavings.
Dress the dish only just before serving, so the arugula stays crisp rather than wilting.
commonMistakes: Slicing the bresaola too thick, which makes it harder to eat and less delicate.
Over-dressing with too much oil or lemon, which can overwhelm the meat's subtle flavor.
Using pre-shredded, low-quality Parmigiano instead of a good wedge, shaved fresh.
servedWith: A light red or white wine
healthBenefits: Bresaola is a lean, low-fat source of protein and iron.
culturalNote: Bresaola is a protected specialty of the Valtellina valley in Lombardy, its cool alpine climate ideal for the slow air-curing process that gives the beef its delicate character.
